questions: Is the cost of swapping P_i and P_{i+1} always exactly i, regardless of the values being swapped or the current state of the permutation?
Does 'sort P in ascending order' mean the final permutation must be (1, 2, ..., N) exactly, or just non-decreasing (which for a permutation is the same)?
If multiple sequences of swaps achieve the sorted order, are we allowed to choose any sequence, or must we find the minimum total cost across all possible sequences?
Is the cost incurred per swap additive, and are we allowed to perform swaps in any order, including revisiting the same index i multiple times?
Should the solution consider that swapping P_i and P_{i+1} with cost i might be more expensive than moving an element through a longer path of cheaper swaps, and thus we need an optimal strategy?
Are we allowed to swap non-adjacent elements directly, or only adjacent swaps as described?
Does the cost i refer to the position index before the swap, after the swap, or is it fixed based on the chosen i regardless of how the permutation changes over time?
If N is large (up to 2e5), is the expected solution time complexity O(N log N) or better, and should we avoid naive algorithms?
